clock.interpretation: No progressive clock or gait slowdown observed over 45 seconds in level3 with six animals. Mixer clocks advanced approximately one second per wall second in early and late windows. Sampled travel remains differentiated by authored ordinary pace; 200ms position sampling undercounts turns.

sourceStage: Before lead final contact-shadow/desktop-roster-reserve polish; physics and clock tested on revised fixed-waypoint production build.

visualInspection.observations: Inspected rabbit, deer and tortoise poses at start,15s,30s and45s. Hooves and tortoise feet generally appear supported. Some midstride rabbit poses still read slightly airborne against the strongly displaced directional shadow; no claim that every pose is visually perfect based only on geometric floor metrics.
visualInspection.desktopRoster: All six rows were readable and visible without journal. The right roster partially occluded Tumble during some poses; reported for the prepared camera-reserve polish.
visualInspection.mobileRoster: All six preference, pace and size rows fit in the visible two-column strip at390x844 without opening the journal or horizontal document overflow.
visualInspection.mobilePlacement: Two normal touch captures reached level3. Final on-screen touch placement succeeded; at the far-right spot part of the trap rim is cropped by the viewport, but the visible input was accepted and did not cross a hidden no-drop UI region.
visualInspection.placement: Inspected valid formerly-rejected meadow, invalid marked boundary, and invalid rock-rim screenshots. Preview instructions identified the matching cause; final valid placements succeeded.

harnessNotes: Initial capture setup required waiting for the visible capture-card button after observable mode changed to caught; corrected QA synchronization, no game change.
Initial invalid-drop assertion compared the live arming timer; corrected to compare retained trap coordinates. No45-second sample was repeated.
An initial mobile test coordinate projected just outside390px and was discarded as usable-touch evidence. The final touch run asserts screen bounds and uses an on-screen point.
